inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL application upserts keyed records with ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE and separately reads a deterministic, ordered, limited leaderboard page.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Rewritten as an independently authored bounded leaderboard refresh. INSERT ... SELECT applies a fixed ORDER BY and LIMIT to a staging batch before upserting the selected rows, so one existing key is refreshed and one new key is inserted while lower-ranked rows remain untouched.

fixture_notes: The refresh batch ranks entries 7002, 7001, 7003, and 7004. LIMIT 3 refreshes existing entry 7001, inserts 7002 and 7003, and leaves lower-ranked entry 7004 absent.
determinism_notes: Points descending plus entry ID ascending defines the selected source subset. All keys and values are fixed; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE score_board (entry_id INT PRIMARY KEY, player_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, points INT NOT NULL, tier VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE score_refresh (batch_id INT NOT NULL, entry_id INT NOT NULL, player_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, points INT NOT NULL, tier VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (batch_id, entry_id))

steps.sql: INSERT INTO score_board (entry_id, player_name, points, tier) SELECT entry_id, player_name, points, tier FROM score_refresh WHERE batch_id = 12 ORDER BY points DESC, entry_id LIMIT 3 ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE player_name = VALUES(player_name), points = VALUES(points), tier = VALUES(tier)

checks.sql: SELECT entry_id, player_name, points, tier FROM score_board ORDER BY entry_id
SELECT batch_id, entry_id, player_name, points, tier FROM score_refresh ORDER BY batch_id, entry_id
